newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva Opera's ballet to push for foreign role.
newsitem.headline: Geneva Opera's ballet to push for foreign role.

text.p: Geneva's financially-troubled Grand Theatre, home of the city's opera and ballet companies, said on Friday it would seek wider recognition for its dancers on the international music scene.

The theatre's general manager, Renee Auphan, a former singer and one of only three women in charge of a major opera house, said in a statement she had appointed a new team to head the ballet and push the drive.
One of the aims was to ensure the influence of the Grand Theatre abroad as well as strengthening ties with its Geneva audience.

Auphan, who took over a year ago when her long-time predecessor Hugues Gall moved to the Paris Opera, said she aimed for a "more open programme," including contemporary choregraphers and first productions.
The ballet would perform three world premieres over the next few months
Auphan said she also wanted to revive 20th century works from the choregraphic heritage which had dropped from the repertoire.

The Geneva ballet, first formed at the Grand Theatre in 1838, has long been under the shadow of the company headed by French choreographer Maurice Bejart in Lausanne, 40 miles (60 kms) away along the Geneva lakeshore.

But Auphan, who had a major success in September at the start of the opera season with a widely-hailed performance of "Hamlet" by 19th century French composer Ambroise Thomas, wants to reshape her company's image.
She said she had appointed Swiss designer and dancer Francois Passard and Italian dancer Giorgio Mancini, both of whom have worked with Bejart, as a double team to run the ballet.
They would also organise foreign tours, which she said were essential for promotion of Geneva at the international level.
Passard is administrator of the 24-dancer company and Mancini its artistic coordinator.

French-born Auphan, former director of the Monte Carlo Opera and member of the Paris Opera company, created and ran the Lausanne city opera company from 1983 to 1995, winning wide recognition for imaginative staging.
